subject.title: Browser tool should reject or redact URLs with embedded credentials instead of passing them through

question: Should OpenClaw browser page navigation treat HTTP(S) URLs with embedded username/password userinfo as unsupported and fail fast before dispatch?
rationale: This is a security hardening request, but the fail-fast policy can break existing Basic-auth URL workflows and needs maintainer acceptance before a linked fix lands.

options.title: Fail fast and redact
options.body: Reject credentialed browser navigation URLs before dispatch, redact any surfaced credential-like URL text, and document supported alternatives such as authenticated profiles, cookies, headers, or Playwright credentials.

options.title: Allow with stricter redaction only
options.body: Keep URL-embedded Basic auth working but add stronger log/error redaction, accepting the ongoing browser-runtime pass-through behavior.

options.title: Defer to a larger auth design
options.body: Leave the issue open until browser auth alternatives are designed explicitly, without merging the current fail-fast PR yet.

recommendation.title: Fail fast and redact
recommendation.body: Reject credentialed browser navigation URLs before dispatch, redact any surfaced credential-like URL text, and document supported alternatives such as authenticated profiles, cookies, headers, or Playwright credentials.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser plugin history and current policy-sensitive surface point to steipete as the strongest available routing owner from the inspected history.
